smell: BackgroundCheck spawns a fire-and-forget goroutine that runs runCheck(ctx); printUpdateNotice in cli/root.go waits at most 100ms before returning, so on the happy path the goroutine races to completion and on the slow path it leaks until the process exits. The pattern is intentional (documented in the package doc) but there is no Wait()/Stop() hook a future caller could use to ensure the HTTP call has returned before process exit.
fix_summary: Either document explicitly that the caller must drain ch before Execute returns (already partly documented), or expose a Done() <-chan struct{} so the caller can opt into a synchronous wait at shutdown. Current 100ms + os.Exit pattern is acceptable for a version check but worth a CLAUDE.md entry under a new concurrency section.
rule_source: Go proverb: don't start a goroutine without knowing how it will stop
must_preserve: Caller contract: ch is buffered cap 1 so the goroutine's send never blocks; the OKDCTL_NO_UPDATE_CHECK short-circuit must still produce a zero-result channel.
severity_reason: Documented intentional fire-and-forget per skill §5 must-preserve; surface as advisory only. Goroutine terminates within httpTimeout (4s) so upper bound on the leak is finite.

smell: promptForConfirmation spawns a reader goroutine that blocks on bufio.Reader.ReadString, races against ctx.Done, and on ctx cancel the goroutine remains blocked on Stdin.Read until the user presses enter or the process exits. Thoroughly documented in the function header, and the capacity-1 inputCh means the goroutine's eventual send never deadlocks — but this is still an unowned goroutine whose lifetime is bounded only by the parent process.
fix_summary: Go 1.25 has no portable cross-platform stdin cancellation; the current design is the least-bad option for a CLI prompt. Document this pattern in CLAUDE.md as the repo-sanctioned approach so future authors copy it verbatim instead of re-inventing. Alternative: use golang.org/x/term.ReadPassword on a separate FD for cancellable input, but that trades one tradeoff for another.
rule_source: Go proverb: don't start a goroutine without knowing how it will stop
must_preserve: Documented behaviour: ctx.Done returns immediately; goroutine lives until user input or process exit; capacity-1 send is non-blocking.
severity_reason: Per skill §5 must-preserve, intentional decouplings flag as suggestion only. The leak is bounded by process lifetime and the design is thoroughly justified inline.

smell: MonitorInstallation spawns a goroutine holding installCmd.Wait(). On ctx cancel the function calls killInstall, waits up to 30s via reapTimer for Wait() to return, then abandons — leaving the goroutine still blocked on the (now-killed) process's Wait() until the OS reaps it. The buffered cap-1 installDone channel prevents the orphaned goroutine from deadlocking when it eventually sends, and sync.Once around killInstall is idempotency-by-construction. This is careful code, but the 30s reap window is still a potential leak if openshift-install ignores SIGKILL.
fix_summary: Pattern is sound. Optional improvements: (a) promote the reap-with-deadline pattern to a shared helper in internal/distribution/okd/phase/ since the same shape will recur elsewhere (e.g. WaitForBootstrap); (b) log the final installCmd.Wait() result in a deferred cleanup goroutine that drains installDone so errors don't vanish. Neither is required — the current code is idiomatic Go 1.25 and ships-safe.
rule_source: Go proverb: a little copying is better than a little dependency
repo-counter-example: same file uses sync.Once + buffered chan correctly
must_preserve: sync.Once guard on Process.Kill (future multi-signal safety); buffered cap-1 installDone channel (prevents send deadlock when abandoned); reapTimer + ctx.Err wrapping for taxonomy-preserving error returns.
severity_reason: Leak window bounded at 30s + OS reap time; code is well-commented and already follows the canonical reap idiom. Flag as suggestion so future authors see the pattern.

smell: WaitFor is a poll loop with ticker, optional timer-based timeout, and ctx.Done race — core concurrency logic with no dedicated tests. Go 1.25's testing/synctest can make this deterministic by running the poll in a synthetic time bubble, letting tests assert exact tick counts and timeout boundaries without real sleeps.
fix_summary: Add TestWaitFor tests under internal/system using testing/synctest.Run to exercise: (a) timeout with no ctx cancel, (b) ctx cancel mid-poll, (c) simultaneous timeout+ctx cancel (ctx-wins invariant), (d) check() returns true on first/Nth iteration. This converts a currently-untested time-sensitive primitive into a deterministic test suite and validates the ctx-preferred-over-timeout invariant the code claims.
must_preserve: The ctx-wins semantics (lines 64-67 and 75-78) — if ctx is cancelled simultaneously with the timeout or tick, the ctx error must be returned, not the timeout error.
severity_reason: No-risk test addition; flags a specific Go 1.25 capability the repo already has in scope.

smell: MonitorInstallation has a ticker-driven CSR-approval loop, a reap timer, and ctx.Done/DeadlineExceeded paths — exactly the shape testing/synctest is designed for. Currently untested because real-time tests would take minutes.
evidence:
ticker := time.NewTicker(opts.CSRApprovalInterval)
// ...
reapTimer := time.NewTimer(30 * time.Second)
select {
case <-installDone:
	reapTimer.Stop()
case <-reapTimer.C:
	p.Log.Warn("install: process did not exit after kill, abandoning reap")
fix_summary: Extract the select-loop body into a testable helper (csrApprovalLoop(ctx, ticker, installDone, k8sClient)) and cover the three exit paths (installDone success, installDone timeout-error, ctx cancel → kill → reap) with testing/synctest. Requires a k8sClient fake; this is the same fake audit-tests will flag as missing.
must_preserve: Behaviour: on ctx cancel, kill → 30s reap → abandon; on installDone non-nil, wrap the error with ctx.Err when ctx.Err is Canceled/DeadlineExceeded so exit-code mapping stays correct.
severity_reason: No-risk test addition; flagged together with the other synctest opportunity so a config-bug aggregation can schedule both under one PR.

smell: CLAUDE.md has no repo-specific concurrency rules. The codebase contains five canonical goroutine patterns (signal-handler on sigCh, spinner, update-check fire-and-forget, stdin reader with ctx race, cmd.Wait reap-with-deadline) that future contributors will copy. Without a CLAUDE.md anchor they will re-invent variants and drift from the documented idioms.
fix_summary: Add a short §Concurrency section to CLAUDE.md covering: (1) no goroutine without a stop signal or documented leak bound (Uber §Goroutine Lifetime); (2) prefer errgroup over WaitGroup when errors must bubble; (3) time.Sleep in retry loops is banned — use ctx.Done select (already the repo convention via wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext); (4) context.Background()/TODO() in production code requires a justification comment; (5) reference internal/distribution/okd/install/monitor.go:65-142 as the canonical cmd.Wait reap-with-deadline example and internal/tui/spinner.go:19-56 as the canonical ticker-backed background worker.
rule_source: Go proverb: don't start a goroutine without knowing how it will stop
must_preserve: CLAUDE.md's existing structure and ~3% comment density guidance.
severity_reason: Policy finding; no code risk. Prior audits (security, subprocess) already depend on CLAUDE.md-level anchors — adding concurrency parallels that.

smell: execute() spawns a signal-watcher goroutine that blocks on <-sigCh forever on the happy path; signal.Stop(sigCh) is deferred but does not close the channel, so on clean exit the goroutine never returns and is only reaped by process exit. Behaviourally identical to confirm.go's documented stdin-reader leak but undocumented here, and less justified because closing sigCh after signal.Stop is mechanical (no blocking I/O involved).
evidence:
sigCh := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
signal.Notify(sigCh, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
defer signal.Stop(sigCh)

ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()

var caughtSig atomic.Value
go func() {
	sig, ok := <-sigCh
	if !ok { return }
	caughtSig.Store(sig)
	cancel()
}()
fix_summary: Two equivalent cleanups, pick one: (a) defer close(sigCh) after signal.Stop so the goroutine's !ok branch actually fires and it returns cleanly; (b) document the process-lifetime leak the same way confirm.go does and cite it from the CLAUDE.md concurrency section proposed in con:6ebdb617. Option (a) is purely additive — close-after-Stop is the Go-documented safe pattern — and removes the only unreaped goroutine in the hot exit path.
rule_source: Go signal package docs: "Stop causes package signal to stop relaying incoming signals to c"
must_preserve: SIGINT/SIGTERM differentiation via caughtSig.Load() — must still populate before cancel() so exit-code mapping reads the right signal.
severity_reason: Leak bounded by process lifetime; ok-branch dead code is a minor smell. Same severity anchor as confirm.go counterpart per skill §5 must-preserve.
